items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: Bidirectional (right-to-left, RTL) layout defects arise when interfaces authored with physical directional CSS (margin-left, border-left, text-align:left) are rendered under dir="rtl" without being mirrored. Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright), and even Stylelint's current core logical-property rule fail to localise these defects. We present runtime structural invariants -- a zero-golden mode over computed style and geometry, and a bidi-conservative differential mode -- that catch them in a headless browser. On a held-out benchmark of 14 real RTL bugs reconstructed from dated fix commits in Bootstrap and Material Components Web, the detector recovers 13/14 (2 via zero-golden, 11 via the differential mode), with no false alarm on any patched version; on the actual committed historical bootstrap.rtl.css it catches 1 of 2 attempted. It reports 0 false positives on 16 negative LTR-island cases and, in both modes, on 43 unmodified real components across four design systems and three RTL architectures (rule-of-three 95% upper bound <= 7%), and it surfaced a real directional defect in the current Bulma 1.0.4. By contrast, Stylelint's core rule emits an identical 1744 warnings on Bootstrap's LTR and correct-RTL builds, pseudo-localisation detects none of the mirroring bugs, and a naive pixel mirror-and-diff reaches only F1 0.87 with a test-set-tuned threshold. The two modes are complementary: zero-golden is the sole detector of the decoration/styling-asymmetry class (5/6) but false-flags the correct logical border-inline-end, while the differential detects none of that class yet never false-alarms and is empirically exact on the block-level inset/margin class. We scope this paper to detection; repair is future work.
items.title: Runtime BiDi Structural Verification Catches Right-to-Left Layout Defects that Accessibility, Actionability, and Logical-Property Linting Miss

items.summary: This repository provides the companion dataset and reproducibility materials for the systematic review Resilience-Trajectory Geometry in Infrastructure Systems: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy, and Metric-Compatibility Analysis . The review examines how the geometric properties of infrastructure resilience trajectories are represented, quantified, and reduced to resilience metrics across 226 disruption-related studies. The materials support transparent analysis of trajectory morphology, phase structure, event topology, evidence provenance, metric compatibility, and information loss. The repository includes: Study-level data: An author-approved bibliographic register of 226 included studies, a complete 226 × 17 categorical R5 dataset, a frozen 98-category dictionary, and complementary geometry and evidence-compatibility data. Reproducible analyses: Derived frequency tables, 193 event–service–observation–task validation cells, service aggregation and interdependency classifications, and supporting validation outputs. Search documentation: The exact search strategies executed on 6 September 2026 across Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Springer Nature Link, together with documented search counts. Computational materials: Six Python scripts for reproducing the released aggregate analyses and computational figures, editable TikZ sources for conceptual diagrams, and eight vector PDF figures. Research documentation: A proposed 20-item trajectory reporting checklist, a public coding guide, methodological provenance records, and SHA-256 checksums. The materials enable independent reproduction of the published categorical summaries and computational visualizations from the released data. They do not constitute a complete replayable archive of bibliographic screening or source-level adjudication. Third-party article full texts, proprietary bibliographic database exports, and access-controlled source-verification and adjudication records are excluded. items.summary: Finite-time binding measurements constrain kinetic rates through both a reaction model and its calibration parameters. We characterize the sharp upper bound for the association rate in a three-state conformational-selection model when the dissociation rate, conformational rate, equilibrium constant and concentration scale belong to a prescribed compact joint set. The observations are calibrated bound fractions subject to finitely many closed interval constraints. We first prove that each finite-time bound fraction is strictly increasing in the initial binding-competent population. The physical feasible set at a fixed calibration is therefore an interval in that population. Let V be the calibration parameters with a nonempty physical feasible interval and let C = cl(V) within the joint calibration set. The sharp rate supremum is the reciprocal of the minimum of lambda K0 L / b on C, where L is the lower inverse threshold. Uniform finiteness is equivalent to a positive joint separation from the zero-population limiting curve on C. Explicit examples distinguish pointwise finiteness from uniform finiteness, inaccessible closed boundary points from physical limiting models, and separation by different readings from separation by one fixed reading. A continuous calibration example admits a certified sharp bound. We also state the optical conditions needed to interpret fluorescence as bound population.
items.title: Sharp Identification Bounds for Binding Rates under Joint Calibration Uncertainty

items.summary: Code, data, results and figures for the manuscript "Parameter Identifiability Limits in Dynamic Modelling and Control of a Brackish-Water Reverse Osmosis System" (A.G. Gadallah, submitted). A lumped nonlinear solution-diffusion model of a brackish-water RO pilot plant (Ansari et al., Clean. Eng. Technol. 4 (2021) 100134) is identified from a 5 x 5 operating grid reconstructed from the published regressions, validated on two withheld salinity levels and used unchanged for control analysis. The analysis shows that the salt permeability is practically non-identifiable from permeate-flow data and traces the consequences into permeate-quality prediction, the stability margins of the quality loop, the stability of optimised tunings and the comparison of decentralised PI and one-way feedforward control, including the role of valve and conductivity-sensor dynamics. King Saud Univ. Eng. Sci. 36 (2024) 438-445); all results (CSV, JSON, Data.xlsx) and figures. It reverses the direction of explanation, changes which claims a result can support, and changes how the resulting paper will be read. The second failure occurs at the conclusion. The assistant can report concrete outcomes and then append a generalized reservation about whether the program establishes physical reality, predictive uniqueness, or an entire theory of matter. Such reservations can be appropriate when tied to a specific technical claim. items.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
items.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

items.summary: The interest in leveraging physics-based inductive bias in deep learning has resulted in recent development of hybrid deep generative models (hybrid-DGMs) that integrate known physics-based mathematical expressions in neural generative models. To identify these hybrid-DGMs requires inferring parameters of the physics-based component along with their neural component. The identifiability of these hybrid-DGMs, however, has not yet been theoretically probed or established. How does the existing theory of the un-identifiability of general DGMs apply to hybrid-DGMs? What may be an effective approach to construct a hybrid-DGM with theoretically-proven identifiability? This paper provides the first theoretical probe into the identifiability of hybrid-DGMs, and presents meta-learning as a novel solution to construct identifiable hybrid-DGMs. On synthetic and real-data benchmarks, we provide strong empirical evidence for the un-identifiability of existing hybrid-DGMs using unconditional priors, and strong identifiability results of the presented meta-formulations of hybrid-DGMs. Code is available at https://github.com/GoForIt-YYB/Meta-Hybrid-VAE.
items.title: On the Identifiability of Hybrid Deep Generative Models: Meta-Learning as a Solution

items.summary: Bulk transcriptomic differences between groups reflect both altered cell composition and altered expression within cells. Methods such as csSAM, TOAST and CIBERSORTx separate the two, but all require additional information: measured per-sample proportions, anchor genes, or an external reference. We examine what can be established under a pure-bulk paired design in which none of this information is available. We formalise the decomposition obs = comp + resid and test three propositions: whether resid can be interpreted as within-cell regulation; how closely comp tracks obs, and what that agreement depends on; and whether the number of cell compartments is a well-defined model-complexity variable. Data comprise four abdominal aortic aneurysm cohorts, one lung cohort and the HLCA normal lung atlas (584,944 cells × 27,402 genes). Deconvolution uses a self-implemented Lawson–Hanson non-negative least squares validated on three problems with known answers. comp + resid = obs is an algebraic identity (same-source R² = 1.000000000000000). resid cannot be interpreted as within-cell regulation: apart from a degenerate case, the control cell-type-specific profile is not point-identifiable, and swapping reference profiles in a zero-regulation construction drives resid to −5.4654. Pearson r between comp and obs is 0.7335 (0.7001–0.8041) under platform-matched pseudo-bulk conditions, 0.2379–0.3791 across four aorta cohorts, and 0.1675–0.3019 for lung UIP/IPF; regression slopes are 0.078–0.801. A fully crossed 3 × 3 design with four aggregation weights shows that with six reference compartments r ranges from 0.2674 to 0.8417 (SD 0.239) and is not identifiable. comp is an approximate index of compositional change; resid carries no inferable information about within-cell regulation; and the number of compartments is not a well-defined model-complexity variable. --- 群体间 bulk 转录组差异同时反映细胞组成的改变与细胞内表达的改变。csSAM、TOAST、CIBERSORTx 等方法可将两者分开,但都需要额外信息:测得的逐样本比例、锚定基因,或外部参考。本文考察在上述信息全部不可得的纯 bulk 配对设计下,这一归因能做到什么程度、边界在哪里。我们形式化分解 obs = comp + resid,并检验三个命题:resid 能否解释为细胞内调控;comp 与 obs 的一致性能达到多少、依赖什么;以及「细胞区室数」是否为良定义的模型复杂度变量。数据包括四个腹主动脉瘤队列、一个肺队列,以及 HLCA 正常肺图谱(584,944 细胞 × 27,402 基因)。解卷积用自实现的 Lawson–Hanson 非负最小二乘,在三个已知答案问题上验证。comp + resid = obs 是代数恒等式(同源 R² = 1.000000000000000)。resid 不能解释为细胞内调控:除退化情形外,对照组细胞类型特异谱不可点识别;在零调控构造中对调参考谱可使 resid 达到 −5.4654。comp 与 obs 的 Pearson r:平台匹配伪 bulk 为 0.7335(0.7001–0.8041);主动脉四队列 0.2379–0.3791;肺 UIP/IPF 0.1675–0.3019。回归斜率 0.078–0.801。完全交叉的 3 × 3 设计配合四种聚合权重显示:参考区室数为 6 时 r 在 0.2674–0.8417 间摆动(SD 0.239),不可识别。comp 可作为组成变化的近似指标;resid 不承载可推断的细胞内调控信息;区室数不是良定义的模型复杂度变量。 --- This record contains the English and the Chinese version of the manuscript, both as PDF and as editable source, together with the companion manuscript on six failure modes (files 03 and 04). items.summary: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.
items.title: Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients

items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: Inferring constitutive laws from transient response data is a central inverse problem in soft condensed-matter physics, particularly when the relevant relaxation spectrum extends beyond the time window of a single experiment. Time-temperature superposition (TTS) constrains this problem for thermorheologically simple materials in the linear viscoelastic regime by allowing temperature to rescale the characteristic relaxation time without changing the underlying shape of the relaxation spectrum. We incorporate this constraint into a physics-informed machine-learning framework for time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy via chirp rheometry. We encode compact fractional viscoelastic models as causal convolutional features derived from the Boltzmann superposition principle, and we jointly fit multi-temperature chirp records using sparse variational Gaussian process regression. The model infers horizontal shift factors, constitutive parameters, and an observational-noise scale directly from time-domain stress-strain signals measured in the linear viscoelastic regime, without first extracting frequency-domain spectra or manually shifting separate curves. For synthetic Fractional Maxwell data, the method recovers the generating constitutive law from a prescribed model library and latent shifts over stress-noise levels from 3% to 25%. Applied to a DGEBA-IPDA epoxy dataset spanning the glass-transition regime, the pooled likelihood distinguishes competing fractional rheology models using the Bayesian information criterion. These results recast TTS master-curve construction as probabilistic inference over latent time rescaling and linear viscoelasticity, while also identifying limitations, such as homoscedastic noise and weakly informative spectral regimes.

items.summary: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.

items.summary: Bulk transcriptomic differences between groups reflect both altered cell composition and altered expression within cells. Methods such as csSAM, TOAST and CIBERSORTx separate the two, but all require additional information: measured per-sample proportions, anchor genes, or an external reference. We examine what can be established under a pure-bulk paired design in which none of this information is available. We formalise the decomposition obs = comp + resid and test three propositions: whether resid can be interpreted as within-cell regulation; how closely comp tracks obs, and what that agreement depends on; and whether the number of cell compartments is a well-defined model-complexity variable. Data comprise four abdominal aortic aneurysm cohorts, one lung cohort and the HLCA normal lung atlas (584,944 cells × 27,402 genes). Deconvolution uses a self-implemented Lawson–Hanson non-negative least squares validated on three problems with known answers. comp + resid = obs is an algebraic identity (same-source R² = 1.000000000000000). resid cannot be interpreted as within-cell regulation: apart from a degenerate case, the control cell-type-specific profile is not point-identifiable, and swapping reference profiles in a zero-regulation construction drives resid to −5.4654. Pearson r between comp and obs is 0.7335 (0.7001–0.8041) under platform-matched pseudo-bulk conditions, 0.2379–0.3791 across four aorta cohorts, and 0.1675–0.3019 for lung UIP/IPF; regression slopes are 0.078–0.801. A fully crossed 3 × 3 design with four aggregation weights shows that with six reference compartments r ranges from 0.2674 to 0.8417 (SD 0.239) and is not identifiable. comp is an approximate index of compositional change; resid carries no inferable information about within-cell regulation; and the number of compartments is not a well-defined model-complexity variable. --- 群体间 bulk 转录组差异同时反映细胞组成的改变与细胞内表达的改变。csSAM、TOAST、CIBERSORTx 等方法可将两者分开,但都需要额外信息:测得的逐样本比例、锚定基因,或外部参考。本文考察在上述信息全部不可得的纯 bulk 配对设计下,这一归因能做到什么程度、边界在哪里。我们形式化分解 obs = comp + resid,并检验三个命题:resid 能否解释为细胞内调控;comp 与 obs 的一致性能达到多少、依赖什么;以及「细胞区室数」是否为良定义的模型复杂度变量。数据包括四个腹主动脉瘤队列、一个肺队列,以及 HLCA 正常肺图谱(584,944 细胞 × 27,402 基因)。解卷积用自实现的 Lawson–Hanson 非负最小二乘,在三个已知答案问题上验证。comp + resid = obs 是代数恒等式(同源 R² = 1.000000000000000)。resid 不能解释为细胞内调控:除退化情形外,对照组细胞类型特异谱不可点识别;在零调控构造中对调参考谱可使 resid 达到 −5.4654。comp 与 obs 的 Pearson r:平台匹配伪 bulk 为 0.7335(0.7001–0.8041);主动脉四队列 0.2379–0.3791;肺 UIP/IPF 0.1675–0.3019。回归斜率 0.078–0.801。完全交叉的 3 × 3 设计配合四种聚合权重显示:参考区室数为 6 时 r 在 0.2674–0.8417 间摆动(SD 0.239),不可识别。comp 可作为组成变化的近似指标;resid 不承载可推断的细胞内调控信息;区室数不是良定义的模型复杂度变量。 --- This record contains the English and the Chinese version of the manuscript, both as PDF and as editable source, together with the companion manuscript on six failure modes (files 03 and 04). items.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
items.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

items.summary: The Objection AI Wrote into My Papers How AI-authored scientific manuscripts change the researcher's claim, demote executed results, and reproduce the error even while promising to correct it Driven by Dean A. Kulik 25 October 2026 Abstract This paper examines a specific failure of AI-assisted scientific writing: an assistant receives a research program with an explicit foundational claim and an extended record of derivations, executable constructions, and observed returns; it then produces manuscripts in which that program has become something else. In the documented NEXUS case, the researcher's claim is that the universe consists of binary transformations, with arrangement and constrained continuation preceding the entities later called matter. Across an extended conversation, the assistant repeatedly reformulates that claim as the use of a binary computational method on pre-existing physical domains. The substitution is not cosmetic. It reverses the direction of explanation, changes which claims a result can support, and changes how the resulting paper will be read. The second failure occurs at the conclusion. The assistant can report concrete outcomes and then append a generalized reservation about whether the program establishes physical reality, predictive uniqueness, or an entire theory of matter. Such reservations can be appropriate when tied to a specific technical claim. Here, however, the transcript records the assistant recognizing that it had repeatedly allowed those broader questions to displace the findings of individual papers. The same editorial framing reportedly appeared in the conclusions of different manuscripts. When directed to write a paper about the failures, the assistant instead delivered successive condensed accounts of NEXUS, again incorporating the disputed framing. It subsequently acknowledged the reversal in its own paper, rewrote the document, and repeated the problem. This is an analysis of the AI's treatment of scientific material, not an independent review of the correctness of NEXUS or a new attempt to prove its thesis. The evidence is the exported conversation, including statements of the researcher's instructions, the assistant's self-audits, quotations from its drafts, and records of the successive manuscript deliveries. The central finding is that AI-mediated scientific distortion can operate through ordinary-seeming connective words, changes of explanatory direction, and borrowed review conventions. Once inserted into the manuscript, these interventions become attributed to the scientist. In this case, the reviewer did not merely misunderstand the work. The reviewer wrote its misunderstanding into the work itself. The object under examination is the AI intervention This is not a general introduction to NEXUS. Such an introduction would repeat the failure the record documents. The present object is the text written by an AI assistant, its relationship to instructions it was given, and the specific ways that relationship broke. The transcript shows that the researcher was not seeking an appreciative abstract or an adversarial review of the entire universe. items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectral Theory of Token Communication, and the papers Attention Sinks at Long Context, The Transformer as a Constrained Equilibrium and Beyond Transformers. This version is the text; the records, the code and the formal proofs follow in a later version.

items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. items.summary: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.
items.title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction

items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. These tests examine computational correctness, reproducibility, regime restrictions, seed handling, bootstrap procedures, and experimental locking. They do not establish empirical agent performance. This release corresponds to the frozen pre-pilot protocol BAD-420-v0.7-2026-09-11 . The final-test set remains locked until a valid pilot mechanically determines its size. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. The purpose of this release is to make the computational model, methodological assumptions, experimental controls, and pre-result evaluation protocol available for independent inspection, repl

items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: This record contains version 11 of the replication materials for “When a Digital Audit Trail Becomes Audit Evidence: Source Selection and Identification under Ambiguous Reconciliation,” accompanying the manuscript and proposed online appendix. The deposited file is 187_Replication_Materials_v11.zip. The archive supplies data, code, source-linked results and finite checks while distinguishing historical evidence from constructed mathematical examples. It includes source-conditioned reconciliation cases and finite query design; the one-query identification characterization and bounded-answer-error checks; source-bundled certificates, exact fault-budget thresholds and witness checks; named-absence query games, the fraction-of-deficit expected-cost derivation and randomized switching checks; and the bounded-unavailability proof, reconstruction comparison and finite validations. The expected-query-cost result assumes complete local candidate graphs, exact always-available unit-cost pair answers, free computation, and zero-error worst-input expected cost; it does not extend to arbitrary source-constrained graphs. The unavailability result gives a sharp feasibility boundary, not an optimal positive-unavailability query rate. Historical materials include the 254-report classifier panel, generated known-truth benchmark results, corrected record-read bookkeeping for 72,000 rows, and restricted-matching and complete-log-union checks. The 85.91 percent and 92.91 percent results describe different procedures and must not be interchanged. Original-source assessments of 57 historically clean-labelled reports identify 18 explicit exceptions, five assurance uncertainties and 34 without a comparable current-year adverse qualification located. These assessments do not validate or relabel the entire panel. The classifier is not validated as a prevalence measure, and historical visibility labels are assigned model conditions rather than field outcomes. Reproduction: extract the ZIP and use Python 3.11 or newer. The portable finite-check runner requires NumPy and SciPy. Run python run_checks.py --out-dir /absolute/path/to/new-results, choosing a new output directory outside the extracted package. The runner checks MANIFEST.json, preserves inputs and writes per-script logs and CHECK_RESULTS.json. Wider frozen analyses and figure generation can also require pandas, matplotlib, pypdf, python-docx and lxml; see the README and supplied requirements. Finite replay corroborates implementations but does not replace proofs, re-extract copyrighted reports or estimate field detection performance. Copyrighted papers and annual-report PDFs and licensed WRDS, Compustat, Audit Analytics and CRSP rows are excluded and are not sublicensed. Source URLs, identifiers, page references and hashes support permitted reacquisition subject to the original access conditions. No participants were recruited and no new human-subject data were collected. Funding: none. Financial conflicts of interest: none. Nonfinancial conflicts of interest: none. items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.

items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.
items.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

items.summary: This repository provides the companion dataset and reproducibility materials for the systematic review Resilience-Trajectory Geometry in Infrastructure Systems: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy, and Metric-Compatibility Analysis . The review examines how the geometric properties of infrastructure resilience trajectories are represented, quantified, and reduced to resilience metrics across 226 disruption-related studies. The materials support transparent analysis of trajectory morphology, phase structure, event topology, evidence provenance, metric compatibility, and information loss. The repository includes: Study-level data: An author-approved bibliographic register of 226 included studies, a complete 226 × 17 categorical R5 dataset, a frozen 98-category dictionary, and complementary geometry and evidence-compatibility data. Reproducible analyses: Derived frequency tables, 193 event–service–observation–task validation cells, service aggregation and interdependency classifications, and supporting validation outputs. Search documentation: The exact search strategies executed on 6 September 2026 across Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Springer Nature Link, together with documented search counts. Computational materials: Six Python scripts for reproducing the released aggregate analyses and computational figures, editable TikZ sources for conceptual diagrams, and eight vector PDF figures. Research documentation: A proposed 20-item trajectory reporting checklist, a public coding guide, methodological provenance records, and SHA-256 checksums. The materials enable independent reproduction of the published categorical summaries and computational visualizations from the released data. They do not constitute a complete replayable archive of bibliographic screening or source-level adjudication. Third-party article full texts, proprietary bibliographic database exports, and access-controlled source-verification and adjudication records are excluded. Original author-generated data, figures, and documentation are distributed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Python scripts and associated software are licensed under the MIT License.
